method: Facts come from each company's own website (home, pricing, feature and FAQ pages) and, for apps, its store listing, read on the checked date. Nothing was signed up for, installed or tried. Prices are quoted as published on that date, in the currency shown. `short` is Winelingo's own wording of those facts, cut to fit a table cell.

dropped.name: WineStaff (winestaff.app)
dropped.why: Its site describes a private app for the staff of its own restaurants; no offer to other venues.

dropped.name: Oeno Academy
dropped.why: Its site said registration was not yet open.

items.name: Winelingo for restaurants
items.what_it_is: A wine course in short lessons that staff take on their own phones, with a weekly team league and one staff test built from the venue's own wine list. Its 13 practice tests, five of them written for floor staff, are free to anyone.
items.best_for: Restaurants, wine bars and hotels that want staff to learn wine itself (grapes, regions, service) and also be tested on the house list.
items.own_wine_list_note: "We build a staff test from your list: ten questions the way guests ask them, each pointing to a bottle you actually pour."
items.manager_tools: None. The business page says: "As the employer you don't get access to anyone's account." A weekly league shows colleagues who have added each other.

price.text: On request: "It depends on the size of your team."
price.free_trial: "New partners start with a free trial period" (length not stated)

limits_or_tradeoffs: No manager dashboard or progress reports: the employer cannot see what each person has completed (source: https://winelingo.app/business/)
The price is not published (source: https://winelingo.app/business/)
The house test is one ten-question test that Winelingo builds by hand from the wine list; it is not regenerated automatically when the list changes (source: https://winelingo.app/business/)
The app is for iPhone; staff with Android phones take the course in a browser and cannot scan labels (source: https://winelingo.app/business/)
New and small: the business page names two partner venues (source: https://winelingo.app/business/)

short.best: Ours: staff learn wine itself, plus one test on your own list
short.own_list: One ten-question test, built for you by hand

items.name: ShiftTrained
items.what_it_is: A browser-based menu and wine training tool that uses AI to turn a restaurant's uploaded menu or wine list into short quizzes staff take on their phones.
items.best_for: Restaurants that want quizzes generated from their own wine list and menu, sent to staff by text link, with pricing tiers by number of employees (up to 20, 40 or 99; more or multi-location is Enterprise).
items.format: web app (SMS link, no install) + AI tool
items.own_wine_list_note: "Upload your wine list PDF, AI generates a full set of questions specific to your bottles, your vintages, your pour costs, your food pairings."
items.manager_tools: Listed on every plan: unlimited manager access, leaderboard and score tracking, inspector-ready reporting, editable AI-generated questions, live Toast and Square sync. Enterprise adds cross-location reporting and a corporate dashboard.
items.languages: "Multi-Language Support" is listed as BETA; no language list is published on the pricing section.

price.text: Basic $29 USD/mo (up to 20 employees); Pro $49 USD/mo (up to 40 employees); Max $99 USD/mo (up to 99 employees); Enterprise (multiple locations or 100+ employees): contact. Yearly billing: "Save 20%".
price.free_trial: "Free trial · No credit card" (length not stated)

limits_or_tradeoffs: Questions are generated from the venue's own list, so it trains staff on the list rather than teaching a general wine curriculum; the company itself contrasts this with "generic wine education". (source: https://www.shifttrained.com/wine-training)
Plans are capped by employee count (20 / 40 / 99); more than one location or 100+ staff requires an Enterprise quote. (source: https://www.shifttrained.com/#pricing)
Multi-language support is marked BETA. (source: https://www.shifttrained.com/#pricing)
Questions are AI-generated; the page says managers can "Change any question you want", which implies review is expected. (source: https://www.shifttrained.com/wine-training)
unverified: Length of the free trial
Which languages the beta multi-language support covers
Whether the $29-$99 plans cover one location only (only Enterprise mentions multiple locations)
The testimonial claim of wine sales "up 34%" is a customer quote on the company's page, not independently checked

short.best: Venues wanting AI quizzes from their own wine list, by text link
short.price: From $29 USD/mo (up to 20 employees); free trial
short.format: Web app via SMS link, no install
short.own_list: AI quizzes from an uploaded list

items.name: My Wine Guide - SommOne Server
items.maker: MWG LLC (country not stated; says staff are "located throughout the US, UK and Australia")
items.what_it_is: A staff training and reference module inside the SommOne wine-list platform, giving servers the venue's live wine list, tasting notes, producer stories and pairings on phones, tablets and PCs.
items.best_for: Restaurants, hotels and clubs that run (or want) a SommOne digital wine list and want staff education tied to that list and its stock; the company cites Wine Spectator award winners and MICHELIN Guide restaurants as its audience.
items.format: web app (Progressive Web App, no app-store download)
items.own_wine_list_note: "Your wine list IS the curriculum. The training updates the moment you add a new vintage or pour."
items.manager_tools: Per-server profiles showing how often and how long staff access SommOne and for what; whether they keep up with alerts, featured wines and pairings; whether they make tasting notes. Alerts and notifications to staff devices; low-stock and out-of-stock updates.

price.text: On request for SommOne Server. Published platform prices: "SommOne Digital Cru Wine List starts at $200/month", "SommOne Inventory and Sales Reporting - $125/month", "SommOne Suite ... starts at $250/month"; "We do not charge any set up fees nor require an upfront commitment."
price.free_trial: No trial stated; the company offers a free "2-day custom demo" built with the venue's own wine list

limits_or_tradeoffs: No separate price is published for SommOne Server; published prices are for the digital wine list, inventory and suite products, and fees are "based on the size of your wine and beverage program". (source: https://www.mywineguide.com/faqs)

The page describes reference content, personal taste profiles, alerts and engagement tracking; it does not describe quizzes, tests or a course structure. (source: https://www.mywineguide.com/restaurant-wine-training)

It is part of a wider wine-program platform (digital list, inventory, POS integrations), so it is not presented as a stand-alone training app. (source: https://www.mywineguide.com/restaurant-wine-training)
The headline guarantee "Sell 30% More Wine — or Your Money Back" is shown without terms on the pages read. (source: https://www.mywineguide.com/restaurant-wine-training)

Terms of the 30% money-back guarantee
Languages supported
Company country of registration

short.best: Venues using a SommOne digital wine list that want staff tied to it
short.format: Web app (PWA) on phones, tablets, PCs
short.own_list: Your list is the curriculum; no quizzes described

items.name: Typsy
items.maker: Typsy (country not stated on the pages read)
items.what_it_is: A hospitality learning platform with 2,000+ short video lessons, including wine courses such as "Wine 101 for servers" (7 lessons, 28m 24s).
items.best_for: Hospitality businesses that want general video training across many roles and topics, with wine as one subject, for teams of up to 100 members (larger is Enterprise).
items.own_wine_list_note: Wine courses are pre-made video courses; the site lists "Custom content" and SmartCards that turn "SOPs and PDFs" into guidance ("NOW IN BETA"), but does not say wine training is built from the venue's wine list.
items.manager_tools: Assign training by role, onboarding stage or need; reporting by team and location; manager portal. The plan comparison lists assigning actions, role-based pathways, operational reporting and workforce visibility as not included in the Individual plan.
items.languages: "Available in 40+ languages"; plan table says "40+ subtitles, 10+ dubbed languages". The Wine 101 for servers page lists English, Spanish, Indonesian and 38 others.

price.text: Individual: €180.00 EUR per year, billed annually (1 user). Team: €120.00 EUR / member / year (up to 100 members). Enterprise (100+ members): Custom. Annual billing "Save 16%"; monthly billing is offered but its price was not read.

items.certificate_or_qualification: Course certificates and badges; the Wine 101 for servers course is stated as recognised by the Institute of Hospitality and worth one CPD point.
limits_or_tradeoffs: Wine is a small part of the library: five wine courses were found in the course list (Wine 101 for servers, Wine knowledge essentials, Introduction to red wine varietals, Introduction to white wine varietals, Champagne essentials) out of "183 courses found". (source: https://www.typsy.com/discover/courses)
Content is general wine and service knowledge on video, not the venue's own wine list. (source: https://www.typsy.com/courses/wine-101-for-servers)
Team pricing is per member per year, so cost scales with headcount. (source: https://www.typsy.com/pricing)
Some enterprise features carry an extra charge: "Enterprise infrastructure (additional fee applies)". (source: https://www.typsy.com/pricing)
unverified: Company country (not stated on the pages read)
Whether the EUR prices are shown to all visitors or localised by region
Monthly-billing prices
Whether a free trial exists
Full count of wine courses (the course list was long; only the first part was fully read)

short.best: Teams wanting broad hospitality video training incl. wine basics
short.price: Team €120.00 EUR per member per year (up to 100)
short.format: Video courses on web, iOS, Android

items.certificate_or_qualification: Vinealto's own awards: Foundation (certificate), Certificate, and Fellowship by examination. These are the company's own awards, not WSET or CMS qualifications.

The course is a general wine syllabus ("47 chapters and nearly 3,000 questions"), not presented as training on a venue's own list. (source: https://vinealto.com/faq)
English only at present. (source: https://vinealto.com/)

Business pricing and bulk discount rates

items.name: Sorso
items.what_it_is: An AI wine-program management platform that generates food pairings, tracks margins and produces an auto-generated nightly staff brief from the venue's menu and wine inventory.
items.best_for: Restaurants that want pairing suggestions, margin tracking and a printed or shared daily briefing for staff rather than a course or quiz tool; integrates with Toast POS.
items.own_wine_list_note: "Import your wine list. Scan labels or import a CSV. Sorso builds your inventory automatically." Staff briefs are generated from this: "Auto-generated nightly staff briefs featuring wine stories, push picks, and talking points".
items.manager_tools: Margin intelligence (profit per bottle and per pour), Toast POS sales and dead-stock view, guest QR wine list. No staff progress tracking, quizzes or reports on staff knowledge are described.

price.text: Starter $99 per month (up to 50 wines in inventory, AI pairings for 1 menu, daily staff brief); Professional $249 per month (unlimited wine inventory, pairings for all menus, Toast POS integration); Enterprise: Custom (multi-location; includes "Staff training sessions").
price.free_trial: "Every plan includes a 14-day free trial. No credit card required."

limits_or_tradeoffs: Staff training here means a daily brief (stories, push picks, talking points); no lessons, quizzes or progress tracking are described. (source: https://sorso.live/)
"Staff training sessions" are listed only under the Enterprise plan. (source: https://sorso.live/)
Starter is limited to 50 wines in inventory and pairings for 1 menu. (source: https://sorso.live/)
The only POS integration named is Toast, and it is on the Professional plan. (source: https://sorso.live/)

Currency of the "$" prices (not named)
What the Enterprise "Staff training sessions" consist of
Marketing figures on the page ("32% avg margin lift", an unnamed New York testimonial) are the company's own claims
Platforms and languages

short.own_list: A nightly staff brief, no quizzes

items.name: WSET Level 1 Award in Wines
items.maker: Wine & Spirit Education Trust (WSET), UK; taught through independent course providers
items.what_it_is: A beginner wine qualification with 6 hours of guided learning, including a closed-book exam of 30 multiple-choice questions, taught in person or online by WSET course providers.
items.best_for: Staff who want a recognised, regulated beginner qualification in general wine knowledge; WSET describes it as for people "new to the world of wine" and does not tailor it to a venue.
items.format: live or in-person course; also online through providers
items.own_wine_list_note: Fixed syllabus: "The main types and styles of wine", common grape varieties, "How to store and serve wine", "The principles of food and wine pairing", and the Level 1 Systematic Approach to Tasting.
items.languages: English, Chinese Traditional, Dutch, French, German, Greek, Italian, Japanese

price.text: Not published by WSET; set by each course provider. Example from one US provider (Napa Valley Wine Academy): $289.00 on-demand online, $329.00 instructor-led online, $425.00 in person.

items.certificate_or_qualification: WSET Level 1 Award in Wines; "regulated by Ofqual, the English regulator for qualifications and exams". On passing: "a digital certificate" and use of the WSET certified logo.
limits_or_tradeoffs: General syllabus; it does not cover a venue's own wine list. (source: https://www.wsetglobal.com/explore-courses/explore-all-courses/level-1-award-in-wines/)
Paid per person through a course provider; WSET does not publish a price. (source: https://www.wsetglobal.com/explore-courses/explore-all-courses/level-1-award-in-wines/)
A one-off course and exam ("closed-book exam of 30 multiple-choice questions"), not ongoing training. (source: https://www.wsetglobal.com/explore-courses/explore-all-courses/level-1-award-in-wines/)
Tasting participation requires legal drinking age in the country of the course. (source: https://www.wsetglobal.com/explore-courses/explore-all-courses/level-1-award-in-wines/)
unverified: Pass mark (not stated on the page read)
Prices at providers other than the one example, and prices outside the USA
WSET's "Training for your team" page was linked but not read
